episode.title: Add bounded provider error details to failed API-call diagnostics
episode.before: At parent commit 45f57c2012b05879339d3a79433b1ca2ed94ff5a, the shared API-call exception handler printed the exception type, provider, model, endpoint, and a cleaned 150-character exception message. Although it already extracted api_error.status_code for recovery decisions, the diagnostic header did not display that status, and it never displayed api_error.body, so request-specific provider explanations could be hidden.
episode.after: At commit 712cebc40f2e156036e55ca313f12fda82e35bff, the shared exception handler appends a truthy status code to the failure header as `[HTTP <status>]`. For HTTP 400 only, it also reads the exception body, converts a nonempty body to text, truncates it to 300 characters, and prints it as a separate Details line. Existing retry, fallback, compression, interruption, and client-error classification behavior remains outside the changed block.
episode.diff: The implementation modifies only run_agent.py with seven insertions and one replacement: it derives a conditional status suffix for the existing failure header and adds a guarded HTTP-400 body-display branch after the cleaned error line. No test file changed, and `git diff --check` reports no whitespace errors.

Both streaming and non-streaming provider requests execute inside the try block handled by this shared exception path, through `_interruptible_streaming_api_call` and `_interruptible_api_call` respectively.

candidate_atomics.name: annotate-failure-with-http-status
candidate_atomics.title: Include available HTTP status in failure diagnostics
candidate_atomics.description: Adapt an API exception's optional status metadata into the primary failure header without changing output for exceptions that lack a usable status.

semantic_action.intent: Make the transport-level failure category immediately visible when a provider request raises an exception.
semantic_action.pre_state: The exception handler has caught a failed provider call and may have extracted a status code, but the primary diagnostic header reports only the exception type.
semantic_action.post_state: When status metadata is truthy, the primary failure header contains the HTTP status; otherwise the header retains its prior shape.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise the shared exception path once with a status-bearing exception and once without status metadata, then assert that only the former header contains the `[HTTP <status>]` suffix. The checked-in diff establishes the formatting rule, but no committed runtime test supplies this oracle.

candidate_atomics.name: surface-bounded-bad-request-body
candidate_atomics.title: Show bounded details for bad-request failures
candidate_atomics.description: Expose a provider's nonempty HTTP-400 response body in a separate diagnostic line while bounding its displayed representation to 300 characters and leaving other statuses unchanged.

semantic_action.intent: Preserve actionable provider explanations for malformed requests or invalid request parameters without emitting an unbounded payload for every failure.
semantic_action.pre_state: A provider call has raised an exception classified with status 400, and useful response-body details may exist outside the cleaned exception message.
semantic_action.post_state: A nonempty HTTP-400 body is converted to text, limited to its first 300 characters, and printed as Details; missing, empty, or non-400 bodies produce no Details line.
semantic_action.validation: Cover four cases: a short nonempty 400 body is printed intact, a body longer than 300 characters is truncated to 300, an empty 400 body is omitted, and a non-400 body is omitted. Source inspection establishes these branches, but the repository contains no committed automated test for them.

candidate_workflows.name: enrich-provider-failure-diagnostics-with-bounded-payload-context
candidate_workflows.title: Enrich provider failure diagnostics with bounded payload context
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution chain for preserving transport status and selectively exposing bounded bad-request details at the shared provider-call error boundary.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure failed provider calls expose enough structured transport and request-error context for diagnosis while keeping payload disclosure conditional and bounded.
when_to_use: A shared provider-call boundary catches exceptions that carry HTTP status metadata not currently shown to the operator.
HTTP 400 exceptions may carry actionable response-body details that are absent from, or lost by cleaning, the ordinary exception message.
Streaming and non-streaming request paths converge on the same exception-diagnostic boundary.
anti_goals: Do not change retry, fallback, authentication refresh, context compression, interruption, or client-error classification policy.
Do not emit response bodies for every HTTP status.
Do not print an unbounded provider payload or replace the existing cleaned summary with the raw body.
Do not treat this diagnostic presentation change as full provider-payload schema normalization.
not_applicable_when: The failure object exposes neither status metadata nor a response body.
The relevant failure is represented as a successful response with an embedded error rather than an exception handled by the shared boundary.
Provider response bodies must not be displayed because the deployment's secrecy or redaction policy prohibits them.
inputs: Caught exception object with optional status_code and body fields
Maximum displayed body length of 300 characters
workflow_graph.entry_state: Provider requests can fail through the shared exception path, but the visible failure header omits available HTTP status and the diagnostic output omits provider response-body details.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The shared boundary displays available HTTP status in the failure header and, only for HTTP 400 with a nonempty body, displays at most 300 characters of body detail without altering downstream recovery decisions.

steps.condition: Apply at the shared exception boundary when formatting the primary failure header; append the suffix only when status metadata is truthy.
steps.validation: Confirm status-bearing failures include `[HTTP <status>]` and failures without usable status metadata preserve the previous header format.

steps.condition: After the cleaned error summary, inspect the body only when the extracted status equals 400; emit Details only for a nonempty body representation.
steps.validation: Confirm short, long, empty, and non-400 body cases satisfy the 300-character and status-selection invariants.

validation_ladder: Inspect the parent state to verify that status and body were previously absent from visible diagnostics.
Inspect the pinned diff to verify conditional status annotation and the HTTP-400-only body branch.
Run `git diff --check` across the exact parent and pinned ref.
Add or execute focused output-capture tests for status present/absent and body short/long/empty/non-400 cases before treating the behavior as runtime-validated.
Exercise both streaming and non-streaming request paths because both feed the shared exception boundary.
stop_conditions: Stop if the exception type does not expose stable status or body metadata and no evidence-backed adapter is available.
Stop or redesign if response bodies can contain secrets and no acceptable redaction policy exists.
Do not claim completion from source inspection alone when automated runtime validation is required by the consuming project.
Stop if implementing the diagnostics would require changing recovery policy, because that is outside this workflow's grounded scope.
unresolved_or_deferred: Focused automated tests are deferred because the pinned resolution contains no test changes or recorded test results.
No redaction or sensitive-field filtering is implemented for the displayed body; only status gating and length bounding are evidenced.
Body conversion uses generic stringification rather than a canonical structured serialization, so ordering and formatting of structured payloads remain provider/runtime dependent.
GitHub PR body, reviews, comments, timeline, and status checks are unavailable in the supplied evidence bundle.

unresolved_questions: Was the absence of automated tests intentional, and what output-capture harness should validate the shared exception path?
Can HTTP-400 response bodies contain credentials, request content, or other sensitive fields requiring redaction before display?
Should structured body objects eventually use a stable serialization format instead of generic string conversion?
